title: Platform systems & services - dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Aisha Martinez
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the platform engineering canonical references for systems & services inventory, Grafana dashboards and alerting policy, standard runbooks, recurring retrospectives outcomes, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as the single source-of-truth for oncall, triage, and platform feature planning.

Scope
- Services covered: platform-api, router, telemetry-ingest, job-worker, cache-proxy, cert-manager, infra-provisioner
- Monitoring: Grafana (preferred dashboards listed below), Prometheus for metrics scraping, Loki for logs, Tempo for traces
- Alerting: PagerDuty for P1/P2, Slack #platform-alerts for P3 notifications

Systems & Services Inventory (summary)
| Service | Owner | Primary SLO | Runbook | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| platform-api | platform-api team | 99.95% availability, p95 latency < 120ms | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-api-runbook | Heavy read traffic; autoscale policy enabled |
| router | infra-networking | 99.9% availability, error rate < 0.5% | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/router-runbook | Global traffic routing; fallback to region-us |
| telemetry-ingest | observability | 99.9% availability, ingestion lag < 30s | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/telemetry-ingest-runbook | Backpressure to clients on overload |
| job-worker | batch-systems | best-effort SLA, job-completion p95 < 10m | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/job-worker-runbook | Uses spot GPUs for batch workloads |
| cache-proxy | infra-caching | 99.9% availability, hit-rate target > 80% | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cache-proxy-runbook | Multi-AZ memcached cluster |

Dashboards and Alerts (operational guidance)

Dashboard catalog (primary):
- Platform Overview (grafana/dashboard/platform-overview): traffic, errors, latency, deployment status
- Ingest & Telemetry (grafana/dashboard/telemetry-ingest): ingestion rate, queue depth, consumer lag, scrape failures
- API Performance (grafana/dashboard/platform-api): p50/p95/p99 latency, request-rate, error budget burn chart
- Router / Network (grafana/dashboard/router): connection rate, 5xx per minute, circuit-breaker events
- Jobs & Batch (grafana/dashboard/job-worker): queued jobs, active jobs, average runtime, preemption rate
- Caching (grafana/dashboard/cache-proxy): hit-rate, evictions, memory usage

Alerting policy (summary of key rules)
1) P1 (pagerduty, immediate phone + Slack) - escalation within 5 minutes
   - platform_api_high_error_rate: 5xx rate > 2% sustained for 2 minutes
   - platform_api_unavailable: http probe failed from 3 regions for 2 minutes
   - prometheus_alertmanager_down: alertmanager target is down for 1 minute
2) P2 (pagerduty, Slack notification) - escalate within 15 minutes
   - high_ingest_lag: telemetry-ingest lag > 60s for 5 minutes
   - router_5xx_spike: 5xx rate > 1% for 10 minutes
   - cache_proxy_evictions: evictions/sec > 50 for 10 minutes
3) P3 (Slack only, follow-up during business hours)
   - elevated_memory: system memory > 85% for 15 minutes
   - minor_job_failures: job-worker failure rate > 5% for 30 minutes

Alert thresholds are tuned quarterly. If you change a threshold, add an entry to the "alert-tuning log" page and notify #platform-observability.

Standard runbook template (use for every service runbook)
1) Impact statement: what does this alert mean for customers?
2) Preconditions / Detection: metrics and log patterns that indicate the issue
3) Triage checklist (quick items):
   - Check Grafana: service dashboard and related panels
   - Check Prometheus: recent rule fires and query results
   - Check Logs (Loki): search for 5xx patterns, exceptions, stack traces
   - Check Traces (Tempo): sample traces for increased tail latency
4) Mitigation steps (ordered):
   a) Rollback last deploy (kubectl rollout undo) if correlated with deploys
   b) Scale up replicas (kubectl scale deployment) or increase provisioned instances
   c) Temporary circuit-breaker / rate-limit rules via router to reduce load
   d) Drain and replace problematic hosts if hardware/memory errors present
5) Post-mortem link: create within 72 hours for P1 incidents

Example CLI snippets (copy into runbooks)
- Check API deployment: kubectl -n platform get deployment platform-api -o wide
- Rollback: kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/platform-api --to-revision=REVISREV
- Increase replicas: kubectl -n platform scale deploy/platform-api --replicas=10
- Restart prometheus: kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart sts/prometheus-server

How-tos and Playbooks (common operational procedures)
- Add a new Grafana panel: follow grafana-managed JSON panels in repo infra/grafana/panels and open PR against infra-configs. Include dashboardId and panel title in PR description.
- Oncall handoff checklist: update runbook links, verify dashboard panels, run quick smoke test (curl /health endpoints), confirm pagerduty escalation policy
- Adding a new alert rule: create a PrometheusRule YAML in infra/monitoring/alerts, include playbook link annotation, and request review from observability team (label reviewers: @observability).

Retrospectives and continuous improvements
- Quarterly retro cadence (end of Q): platform oncall + SRE + owners. Typical outputs: adjust SLO targets, add synthetic checks, deprecate low-signal alerts.
- Recent changes (last retro):
  - Reduced noisy deploy-linked alerts by adding deploy tag correlation (Jun 2026)
  - Added ingestion backpressure mechanism to telemetry-ingest to prevent system-wide cascades (May 2026)
  - Introduced "error budget burn" panel to the Platform Overview dashboard (Apr 2026)

Near-term roadmap (next 6 months)
- Q3 2026:
  - Unified alert management: migrate to prometheus-operator v1.11 and add alert runbook annotations (owner: observability)
  - Synthetic user journeys: implement cross-region synthetic tests for platform-api and router (owner: platform-api)
  - Dashboard refresh: consolidate 3 overlapping panels and add cost-per-request panel (owner: eng-platform dashboards)
- Q4 2026:
  - Auto-remediation pilot: lambda hypervisor that auto-scales and restarts degraded pods based on heuristics (owner: eng-sre)
  - Service dependency graph: generate automated service maps from tracing data (owner: infra-metadata)

Ownership and contacts
- Platform SRE lead: Daniel Cho (daniel.cho@redwood.com)
- Observability: Maya Thompson (maya.thompson@redwood.com)
- Oncall rotation: see /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-schedule
- PagerDuty: Redwood-Platform (service id: PDPLAT1234)

Post-incident process and accountability
- For every P1: owner must create an incident ticket, post an initial incident summary to #platform-incidents within 1 hour, and create a full postmortem within 72 hours.
- P1 postmortems must include: timeline, detection signal, root cause, mitigations, action items with owners and due dates.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-platform/templates/runbook-template
- Grafana dashboard repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-configs.git//grafana
- Monitoring alert examples: infra/monitoring/examples/prometheus-rules.yaml (include standard annotations for runbook and severity)

If you update any of the P1/P2 rules or the platform SLOs, add an entry to the change log and ping the SRE lead for review.
